scope.q: What specific user actions or states define a 'completed setup' versus an 'incomplete setup' within the product?
scope.why: Without a clear definition, we cannot accurately measure the problem or determine if any solution is successful.

scope.q: Beyond the current problematic analytics, what existing logs, database records, or system events could potentially provide a baseline for user progression through setup?
scope.why: Understanding all available data sources, however imperfect, helps us identify starting points and potential data gaps.

scope.q: What is the primary business objective for improving setup completion, e.g., increased conversion to paid, higher initial engagement, or reduced support tickets?
scope.why: This will dictate the success metrics and help prioritize which parts of the setup flow to focus on first.

decomposition.title: Define & Instrument Core Setup Events
decomposition.why: We need to precisely define the critical steps of the setup flow and implement reliable, granular event tracking for each.

decomposition.title: Build Robust Data Ingestion & Storage
decomposition.why: A solid foundation is required to reliably collect, store, and make raw event data accessible for processing.

decomposition.title: Develop Data Transformation & Analytics Pipeline
decomposition.why: Raw events need to be cleaned, structured, and aggregated into a usable format for analysis and reporting.

decomposition.title: Construct Setup Funnel & Drop-off Visualization
decomposition.why: Product needs a clear, actionable view of where users are abandoning setup to validate their theories and identify key problem areas.

decomposition.title: Establish A/B Testing Framework for Interventions
decomposition.why: Once drop-off points are identified, we need a systematic way to test solutions and measure their impact on setup completion.

components.name: User Frontend
components.sub: Application where users perform setup actions.

components.name: Event Tracking SDK
components.sub: Client-side library for capturing user interactions.

components.name: Event Ingestion API
components.sub: API endpoint for receiving raw event data.

components.name: Raw Event Store
components.sub: Persistent storage for all raw, un-processed events.

components.name: ETL Processing Service
components.sub: Transforms raw events into structured analytical data.

components.name: Analytics Data Mart
components.sub: Clean, aggregated data optimized for querying.

components.name: Analytics Dashboard
components.sub: Visualization tool for product team to monitor metrics.

components.name: Experimentation Service
components.sub: Manages A/B test variants and feature flags.

components.name: Product Team
components.sub: Stakeholders consuming insights and defining tests.

sprint.title: Define 'Setup Complete' & Event Schema
sprint.deliv: Documented definition of setup completion, key steps, and a preliminary event tracking schema for each step.

sprint.title: Implement Client-Side Event Tracking
sprint.deliv: Working client-side SDK integrated into the signup/setup flow, sending mocked or test events to a local endpoint.

sprint.title: Setup Event Ingestion & Raw Storage
sprint.deliv: Operational API endpoint accepting events and persisting them to a raw event database; schema validation implemented.

sprint.title: Develop Core ETL Pipeline
sprint.deliv: Initial ETL job transforming raw signup/setup events into a clean, normalized table in the analytics data mart.

sprint.title: Build Basic Funnel Dashboard
sprint.deliv: Interactive dashboard visualizing the signup-to-setup completion funnel, showing drop-off rates at each defined step.

sprint.title: Integrate Experimentation Framework
sprint.deliv: A/B testing service integrated with the frontend, capable of serving different UI variants for a specific test scenario.

sprint.title: Review Data & Plan First Experiment
sprint.deliv: Internal review session with product team to analyze initial funnel data, identify a high-impact drop-off, and define the first A/B test.

risks.risk: Inaccurate or incomplete event tracking due to complex frontend interactions or edge cases.
risks.mitigation: Implement client-side validation, server-side data contract enforcement, and comprehensive end-to-end testing with real user flows.

risks.risk: Product team's initial hypotheses about drop-off points are incorrect or not addressable through simple UI changes.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize initial data collection and visualization to validate or refine hypotheses before investing heavily in specific solutions or experiments.

risks.risk: Performance degradation on the client-side due to excessive or inefficient event tracking.
risks.mitigation: Implement asynchronous event sending, batching mechanisms, and monitor frontend performance metrics closely during and after deployment.

risks.risk: Data privacy or compliance issues if sensitive user information is accidentally captured in events.
risks.mitigation: Conduct a thorough privacy review of all tracked data points, implement data masking/anonymization at the source, and ensure strict access controls on the raw event store.
